headline: 5 Times The Transport Minister's Office Had To Clarify That 'It's Just A Metaphor'
body:
1. When the Minister famously said 'The roads are so smooth you could eat off them,' and his press team spent three days clarifying that he was not literally proposing a mobile, tarmac-based catering service for highway travelers.

2. When he remarked that 'my patience is running on fumes,' which prompted an urgent memo from the logistics wing confirming that no government vehicle was, in fact, currently out of gas or awaiting a fuel pump update.

3. When he described a new flyover project as 'a bridge to the future,' leading the Planning Commission to frantically issue a circular explaining that they are not currently authorized to build portals to the year 2050.

4. When he noted that 'we have hit a speed bump,' causing local civil engineers to dispatch twenty teams to look for physical road damage that did not exist outside of a figurative discussion on policy bottlenecks.

5. When he promised that 'everyone will get a green light,' forcing the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to confirm they were not installing traffic signals in private living rooms across the country.
caption: Context is a lost art. Here is a look at the five times we all collectively took things way too literally. Which one was your favorite? #MinistryLife #ContextMatters #Satire (satire)
igHook: Ever had your words taken completely out of context like this?
